The HKMA participates in several working groups supporting FCLTGlobal’s research into leading market practices for long-term portfolios and the decarbonisation of private assets, as well as the application of such practices by long-term investors. As a member of the NGFS and a supporter of the TCFD, the HKMA contributed to the NGFS Guide on Climate-related Disclosure for Central Banks, demonstrating its commitment to adopting sound ESG practices. The HKMA also leads a workstream under the NGFS’s “Net Zero for Central Banks” workstream, contributing to the development of sustainable and responsible investment approaches for the central banking community. The HKMA continues to participate in various industry forums and seminars to share insights on responsible investment and climate change strategies. Ms Clara Lau, Chief Risk Officer of the Exchange Fund Investment Office (centre), speaks at a sharing session on ESG investment opportunities Building internal capabilities is critical to continuing the ESG journey. In addition to encouraging staff to take sustainability-related courses and obtain relevant qualifications, the HKMA has gained relevant knowledge and practical experience since 2021 through the process of engaging external consultants to advise on leading industry practices for portfolio climate transition. The HKMA also uses ESG data compiled by reputable external data providers to supplement its ongoing portfolio analysis, helping to strengthen the Exchange Fund’s ESG resilience.

The HKMA is committed to reducing its organisational carbon footprint, with the aim of achieving net-zero emissions by 2050 or earlier and contributing to Hong Kong’s overall climate goals. While striving to promote environmental sustainability, the HKMA also fulfils its commitments to caring for staff well-being, promoting financial inclusion and discharging social responsibility. The HKMA is committed to conducting its daily operations in a responsible and sustainable manner. To this end, the HKMA puts sustainability principles into practice under the three pillars of the environment, employees and social responsibility (Chart 1). The Corporate Social Responsibility and Sustainability Committee is responsible for leading the formulation and implementation of the HKMA’s sustainability strategy. Chaired by the Chief Executive of the HKMA, the Committee comprises three Deputy Chief Executives and representatives from the Risk and Compliance Department and the Corporate Services Department, and reports regularly to the Governance Sub-Committee under the Exchange Fund Advisory Committee. Under the Committee’s leadership, various teams and working groups are responsible for planning and implementing measures in their respective areas. In 2022, the Corporate Social Responsibility and Sustainability Committee approved the climate targets for corporate operations and reviewed the transition roadmap for achieving net-zero emissions by 2050 or earlier. During the year, the Committee continued to review the progress of the HKMA’s green initiatives, including proposals to enhance its sustainable procurement policies, procedures and approaches. Sustainability governance structure The HKMA’s corporate sustainability journey In recognition of the HKMA’s commitment to caring for the environment, its employees and the wider community, the Hong Kong Council of Social Service awarded the HKMA the “15 Years Plus Caring Organisation” logo for the 16th consecutive year. The HKMA attaches great importance to its organisational carbon footprint and has formulated internal Green Office Guidelines to manage the environmental impact of its operational processes. The HKMA has incorporated environmental considerations into the interior design, operation and maintenance of its offices. In 2022, BEAM Plus awarded the HKMA a Gold rating for certain renovated office areas. This was the second green building certification obtained by the HKMA, following the LEED Gold certification awarded in 2021. Awarded a Gold rating under BEAM Plus Interiors Version 1.0 The HKMA implemented various energy-saving measures. Total energy consumption6 in 2022 was 4,996.4 megawatt-hours (2.8 megawatt-hours per person7), representing a decrease of 24.4% from 2015 (Chart 1). Total Scope 1 and Scope 2 greenhouse gas emissions8 in 2022 were 2,996.4 tonnes of carbon dioxide equivalent (tCO2e) (1.7 tCO2e per person), representing a decrease of 38.2% from 2015 (Chart 2). Chart 1 Chart 2 Greenhouse gas emissions intensity (Scopes 1 and 2) The HKMA encourages paperless internal operations. It has also implemented a print management system under which staff must log in to the printer to confirm each print request, helping reduce unnecessary printing and toner use. Where printing is necessary, double-sided and black-and-white printing is encouraged. The HKMA is also preparing to implement an internal electronic records management system. Total paper consumption in 2022 was 20.5 tonnes (0.0114 tonnes per person), representing a decrease of 65.3% from 2015 (Chart A). Chart A: Paper consumption intensity The HKMA’s waste management efforts continued to follow the “4R” principle. In addition to conventional waste, the HKMA also reduces electronic waste by adopting technological solutions such as server virtualisation and private cloud infrastructure. In 2022, the HKMA engaged an external company for the first time to conduct a waste audit analysing the composition of office waste. The audit found that food waste accounted for a significant proportion of total waste, prompting the HKMA to launch a food waste recycling programme (see “Enhancing waste management” on page 41). The total amount of non-hazardous waste generated in 2022, including general waste and recyclables, was 242.0 tonnes (0.135 tonnes per person), representing a decrease of 4.8% from 2015 (Chart 3). The fluctuations in the trend were mainly attributable to work-from-home arrangements implemented during the peak of the COVID-19 pandemic and the resumption of office operations after the fifth wave of the pandemic. Chart 3 Non-hazardous waste intensity The HKMA gives priority to waste reduction at source and is committed to reducing, reusing and recycling. In 2022, the HKMA engaged a company for the first time to conduct a waste audit to better understand the composition of waste from its daily operations (plastics, paper, metals, glass, wood, electronics, etc.) and provide waste reduction recommendations. Based on the audit findings, the HKMA launched a food waste recycling programme in November, placing food waste collection bins in all pantries. Food waste collected each day is transported to an organic resources recovery centre in Hong Kong and converted into renewable energy for electricity generation. Residues from the conversion process can also be made into compost for landscaping and agricultural production. Recycling bins are also conveniently located throughout the offices. The HKMA shares recycling tips with staff and places greater emphasis on further improving source separation of recyclables and precautions for handling recyclable items such as cardboard boxes, food containers and beverage bottles. In addition, we continue to organise activities to raise staff’s environmental awareness, explain waste management policies and encourage staff to make good use of the recycling facilities in the offices. Food waste collected daily is transported to an organic resources recovery centre Recycling plastic items The HKMA operates two data centres, one for operations and the other for backup. As they account for a major share of the organisation’s overall energy consumption, the HKMA has adopted green designs and various energy-saving measures, including in-row air-conditioning systems, light-emitting diode lighting and round-the-clock monitoring of power-use efficiency. Following the completion of a consultancy study on the green performance of these data centres in 2022, the HKMA is preparing to implement recommendations to improve overall energy efficiency. It has also begun preparations to obtain green data centre certification. The HKMA recognises the importance of building a culture of sustainability and therefore regularly launches various programmes and activities to educate and encourage staff to develop sustainable habits and adopt green and digital ways of working. The HKMA shares green living tips and annual office-wide energy and paper consumption statistics with staff, reminding them to help address environmental issues at the individual level. Staff are also encouraged to make suggestions on sustainability matters. Led by a Senior Manager in the Administration Division, a task force brings together staff from different departments to brainstorm ideas and specific measures for promoting a green workplace. Task force members also serve as ambassadors when new green initiatives are launched. The HKMA encourages the wider community to adopt more environmentally friendly practices and has introduced various measures to enhance the operational efficiency of the HKMA, the financial industry and the economy as a whole while minimising resource consumption. The HKMA’s Submission Through Electronic Transmission system (STET) is a one-stop platform through which banks submit documents electronically to the HKMA, covering various periodic returns required weekly, monthly, quarterly or annually. Another system, e-Delivery, is a secure electronic communication channel through which the HKMA issues information such as circulars and guidelines to banks. The two systems help save a substantial amount of paper each year. In handling banking complaints and enforcement work, the HKMA has taken measures to support paperless document submission, allowing bank customers to lodge complaints through electronic channels and online forms. The HKMA is also developing a new-generation management information system to facilitate complaint handling and the transition from paper-based to digital records. To reduce paper consumption, the Central Moneymarkets Unit (CMU)9 has adopted digital signatures in its daily communications with participants, including the issuance of circulars, account-opening and account-termination letters, and responses to audit confirmations. Looking ahead, the CMU will continue to explore further green initiatives, including automated electronic processes for internal and external communications. By promoting the use of the Faster Payment System (FPS) and stored value facilities, the HKMA encourages the public to make greater use of electronic payment methods in place of cash and physical cheques. Further information on the FPS and stored value facilities is provided in the chapter “Hong Kong’s International Financial Centre Status” of the HKMA Annual Report 2022. Distributing electronic lai see is simple and convenient and reduces the use of physical lai see envelopes and banknotes, thereby supporting Hong Kong’s sustainable development. To this end, the HKMA continued to promote actively across various social media and traditional platforms, encouraging the public to distribute electronic lai see during the Lunar New Year through the FPS or other e-wallet services via online or mobile banking. Major banks and e-wallet operators also organised various activities to encourage users to send electronic lai see, such as offering festive user interfaces, enhancing functionality for greater convenience, and launching lucky draws or cash rebates. The HKMA promotes electronic lai see on social media For members of the public who choose to distribute physical lai see during the Lunar New Year, the HKMA continued to encourage them to use “good-as-new notes”, which are used but still in good condition. The use of good-as-new notes reduces the need to print new banknotes, thereby lowering the environmental impact. Feedback from note-issuing banks indicates that the public has become increasingly receptive to good-as-new notes in recent years. The Coin Collection Programme reflects the HKMA’s efforts to promote coin recycling. Coins collected under the Programme are recirculated to meet public demand, enhancing the efficiency of coin circulation and reducing the need for minting. The Programme operates two Coin Carts and has so far served more than 1 million customers, collecting more than 800 million coins with a total face value of approximately HKD1.3 billion. In 2022, around 78% of users chose to use some or all of the value of their coins to top up their stored value facility accounts. The HKMA has maintained its collaboration with the Hong Kong Council of Social Service, deploying Coin Carts to collect coins on flag days organised by non-governmental organisations in support of social services. Coin-counting machine on a Coin Cart Launched in 2014, the Coin Collection Programme is the world’s first systematic coin collection programme using a mobile vehicle concept. Over the years, it has received multiple local and international awards in recognition of its innovative and environmentally friendly approach to coin handling. The Programme operates two Coin Carts, each equipped with two high-speed coin-counting machines to collect coins exchanged by the public. Members of the public may choose to exchange their coins for banknotes, use them to top up stored value facility accounts such as Octopus cards or e-wallets, or donate them to The Community Chest. In addition to collecting coins, the Coin Carts are occasionally deployed for various educational activities, such as student visits.

Hong Kong Quality Assurance Agency conducted an independent verification of the climate targets (“Climate Targets”) of the Hong Kong Monetary Authority (“HKMA”). The Climate Targets were developed with reference to the requirements of the SBTi Corporate Manual (“SBTi Corporate Manual”). The purpose of this verification was to verify whether the Climate Targets were developed with reference to the SBTi Corporate Manual. The verification was conducted in accordance with International Standard on Assurance Engagements 3000 (Revised), “Assurance Engagements Other than Audits or Reviews of Historical Financial Information”, issued by the International Auditing and Assurance Standards Board. The verification procedures were designed to form an opinion and conclusion to obtain a reasonable level of assurance. The verification process was determined in accordance with the requirements of the SBTi Corporate Manual. The HKMA is responsible for the collection and presentation of the information. Our verification work was conducted with absolute independence and impartiality. Based on the results of this verification, Hong Kong Quality Assurance Agency provides reasonable assurance and concludes that: • The Climate Targets were developed with reference to the SBTi Corporate Manual. Shum Siu Yan Audit Head Hong Kong Quality Assurance Agency March 2023 Verification Statement Hong Kong Quality Assurance Agency conducted an independent verification of the 2022 environmental data (“2022 Data”) of the Hong Kong Monetary Authority (“HKMA”). The 2022 Data comprise total energy consumption, Scope 1 and Scope 2 greenhouse gas emissions intensity, paper consumption intensity, non-hazardous waste generation intensity and recycling rate for 2022, as well as changes in these data compared with 2015 levels. The HKMA’s greenhouse gas emissions data were compiled in accordance with the Greenhouse Gas Protocol (“GHG Protocol”) jointly issued by the World Resources Institute (“WRI”) and the World Business Council for Sustainable Development (“WBCSD”). The scope of verification covered the relevant data for the period from 1 January 2022 to 31 December 2022, as well as the relevant data for the period from 1 January 2015 to 31 December 2015 used for annual performance comparison. The scope of verification covered a total of 6 office and warehouse premises, comprising 4 offices at 1) Two International Finance Centre, 2) Hopewell Centre, 3) One Pacific Place, and 4) Kowloon Commerce Centre, and 2 warehouses at 5) Roxy Industrial Centre and 6) Zung Fu Centre, located in Kwai Chung and Tsuen Wan respectively. The purpose of the verification was to provide reasonable assurance as to the accuracy and reliability of the 2022 Data and to confirm the adequacy of the HKMA’s data collection mechanism. Within the scope of verification, Hong Kong Quality Assurance Agency examined representative data and supporting evidence selected from the 6 premises. The verification was conducted in accordance with International Standard on Assurance Engagements 3000 (Revised), “Assurance Engagements Other than Audits or Reviews of Historical Financial Information”, issued by the International Auditing and Assurance Standards Board. The verification procedures were designed to form an opinion and conclusion to obtain a reasonable level of assurance. The verification process was determined in accordance with the requirements of the GHG Protocol. The verification process tested the completeness and accuracy of the data by tracing selected sample data to their sources, and reviewed and reliability-tested the underlying procedures for data collection, aggregation, estimation, calculation and internal checking. The verification process also included verifying the internal data collection and management mechanisms, interviewing representatives responsible for preparing the 2022 Data, and examining selected representative data and information. The relevant source data and supporting evidence were also reviewed in detail during the verification process. The HKMA is responsible for the collection and presentation of the information. Our verification work was conducted with absolute independence and impartiality. The verification team of Hong Kong Quality Assurance Agency was not involved in the preparation of the 2022 Data. Based on the results of this verification, Hong Kong Quality Assurance Agency provides reasonable assurance regarding the 2022 Data and concludes that: • The 2022 Data are materially accurate and reliable; • The HKMA’s overall data collection mechanism is adequate. Shum Siu Yan Audit Head Hong Kong Quality Assurance Agency March 2023

Scaling up and accelerating climate action has become the most pressing issue of our time. Nearly half of the critical decade for addressing the climate crisis has already passed. We need to reduce global carbon emissions by more than 40% within this decade to have a chance of limiting global warming to within 1.5 degrees Celsius. Yet greenhouse gas emissions have repeatedly reached record highs. The latest climate science indicates that the window for limiting the rise in global temperature to within 1.5 degrees Celsius will soon close. The impacts of a 1.1-degree Celsius rise are already clearly felt by everyone—extreme weather events, including record-breaking heatwaves and droughts, severe flooding and storms, are occurring more frequently across the globe and becoming increasingly intense. Hong Kong is no exception. Last September, immediately after being battered by a powerful super typhoon, we experienced a once-in-a-century rainstorm. Despite our sound infrastructure and ability to respond swiftly to disasters, the impacts were still very severe—widespread flooding, traffic disruption and damage to roads in many locations. All these are stark reminders that decisive and ambitious climate action brooks no delay. Asia faces particularly formidable challenges on its journey towards a low-carbon transition, especially in balancing economic development and sustainability. We need credible transition strategies that strike an appropriate balance between climate action, economic growth and social inclusion. This is by no means easy. Driven by rapid economic development and population growth, the region accounts for more than half of global carbon emissions. At the same time, the Asia-Pacific region is densely populated and, because of its geographical location, vulnerable to sea-level rise and extreme weather. As the economies in the region are at different stages of development, while the low-carbon transition will create new opportunities for some, raising the necessary transition finance will be a tremendous challenge for others. Market estimates suggest that the Asia-Pacific region will require more than US$3 trillion in low-carbon transition investment annually over the next 30 years. As an international financial centre, Hong Kong has both the capability and the responsibility to harness the power of finance to support the low-carbon transition across Asia. As a banking regulator, market facilitator and responsible investor, the HKMA has devoted significant efforts to the sustainability agenda. The chapters of this report set out the various concrete measures and initiatives undertaken by the HKMA over the past year. In addition, to strengthen the HKMA’s internal governance framework and more effectively co-ordinate sustainability work across different functions, we established the Green and Sustainability Steering Committee last year. For details of the Steering Committee, please refer to the new chapter entitled “Sustainability Governance”. Hong Kong banks play an important role in supporting Asia’s transition to net zero. In addition to performing our traditional role as banking regulator by ensuring through our day-to-day supervision that banks properly manage climate risk, we also serve as a facilitator to support the banking sector in financing the low-carbon transition. One example is the development of a green classification framework to help banks and other financial institutions identify environmentally sustainable activities, thereby aligning their business decisions with global climate goals. We launched a prototype green classification framework for consultation in May and are now refining the framework in light of the feedback received. Moreover, as the need for higher-quality and more globally comparable sustainability disclosures grows, the HKMA is working with other regulators to develop a clear roadmap for Hong Kong to adopt the disclosure standards issued by the International Sustainability Standards Board in June, which constitute a comprehensive global baseline for sustainability reporting. The HKMA’s role as a facilitator extends beyond developing frameworks and rules; we are also committed to addressing industry pain points. At present, data limitations make it difficult for many banks to conduct physical risk assessments. In view of this, the HKMA will shortly launch a cloud-based physical risk assessment platform. By simply entering a property address, banks will be able to assess the impact of physical hazards on residential and commercial buildings in Hong Kong under different climate scenarios, helping them manage the associated climate risk. As a leading international financial centre and sustainable finance hub in Asia, Hong Kong has long served as a bridge channelling international investment into sustainable projects in Asia to support the region’s low-carbon transition. In recent years, international green and sustainable bonds arranged in Hong Kong have accounted for more than one-third of the Asian market, significantly ahead of other jurisdictions. Particularly noteworthy is that the Shenzhen Municipal Government and the Hainan Provincial Government issued green and sustainable bonds in Hong Kong in 2023 for the third and second consecutive years respectively, once again affirming Hong Kong’s important role as a green gateway connecting the Mainland with the rest of the world. The vibrant development of Hong Kong’s sustainable bond market is attributable in part to the demonstration effect of the Government Green Bond Programme. Since 2019, the HKMA has assisted the Government in issuing approximately US$25 billion of green bonds to institutional and retail investors. We have seized every issuance opportunity to innovate and broaden the features of green bonds, including currencies, tenors and distribution channels, laying the groundwork for other public- and private-sector green bond issuers in the region. Following the issuance of the world’s largest government retail green bond in 2022, we issued one of the world’s first government tokenised green bonds in February 2023. In February 2024, we completed the second issuance of tokenised green bonds. Denominated in 4 major currencies and issued in digitally native form, they were the world’s first multi-currency digital green bonds. Meanwhile, we have also proactively introduced various measures to enhance the vibrancy and competitiveness of Hong Kong’s sustainable finance ecosystem. These encompass work in multiple areas, including skills training, data enhancement, green fintech and transition finance. In talent development in particular, we introduced a new “Green and Sustainable Finance” module under the Enhanced Competency Framework for Banking Practitioners in 2023, providing banking practitioners with a structured curriculum to deepen their understanding and professional knowledge of green and sustainable finance. Transition finance is another key focus of our work. It finances decarbonisation activities in high-carbon and hard-to-abate sectors, preventing these sectors from failing to transition because of a lack of financial support. To support the sound development of transition finance, the HKMA will expand Hong Kong’s green classification framework to cover transition activities. We will also extend the scope of the Green and Sustainable Finance Grant Scheme, which provides grants to eligible bond issuers and borrowers, to include transition bonds and loans, encouraging enterprises in the region to raise transition finance in Hong Kong. In addition, we will strengthen engagement with relevant stakeholders and attract private-sector investment into sustainable projects that have historically faced financing difficulties through public-private partnerships and blended finance. Some of the above work requires cross-sector collaboration and is primarily co-ordinated by the Green and Sustainable Finance Cross-Agency Steering Group, co-chaired by the HKMA and the Securities and Futures Commission. Regional collaboration is equally important. In addition to our longstanding collaboration with the International Finance Corporation on the Alliance for Green Commercial Banks, the HKMA’s Infrastructure Financing Facilitation Office also joined the Capacity-building Alliance of Sustainable Investment and the Green Investment and Finance Partnership as a founding member in 2023. The Glasgow Financial Alliance for Net Zero also announced plans to establish a chapter in Hong Kong. Through these partnerships, we hope to promote skills development and knowledge sharing, thereby supporting the channelling of capital into sustainable projects across the region and around the world. To foster new business development and knowledge exchange, the HKMA also helped organise the inaugural Hong Kong Green Week earlier this year. It attracted more than 1,600 guests from nearly 30 jurisdictions, including leading global decision-makers in business and finance, to discuss ways to scale up climate finance in the region and forge new partnerships. Chief Executive Mr Eddie Yue delivered remarks at the Climate Business Forum: Asia Pacific, the flagship event of Hong Kong Green Week. As the manager of Hong Kong’s official reserves and a major global asset owner, the HKMA leads by example as a responsible investor. Since 2015, the HKMA has been at the forefront of investing in green and sustainable assets and has gradually expanded the Exchange Fund’s portfolios of ESG and green assets in the public and private markets. In pursuit of the goal of achieving net-zero emissions for the Exchange Fund’s “Investment Portfolio” by 2050 or earlier, the HKMA added an actively managed global equity portfolio focused on sustainability and climate transition last year, while extending the application of a customised low-carbon equity index to another public-market portfolio. In addition, the green, social and sustainability bonds prioritised by the HKMA outperformed their investment benchmarks, demonstrating the proposition of “doing well by doing good”. In the private markets, we continued to pursue green-related investment opportunities and became an anchor investor in two Asia-focused transition investment funds. At the end of 2022, the weighted average carbon intensity (WACI) of the Exchange Fund’s equity portfolios was 6% and 46% lower than the levels in 2021 and 2017 respectively, and remained below the overall market level. As a sustainable organisation, the HKMA will continue to strive for improvement, setting our sustainability goals and plans around the three pillars of environmental, employee and social responsibility. Specifically, on our journey towards a low-carbon transition, the HKMA continues to strengthen its capacity to address climate change by assessing our environmental performance and implementing various internal measures. These measures encompass emissions reduction, energy efficiency and waste management, with the ultimate objective of fulfilling our commitment to achieve net-zero emissions by 2050 or earlier. We have developed plans to eliminate Scope 1 emissions entirely in the near term and are making good progress towards our medium-term target of reducing Scope 2 emissions by 2030. To attract and retain outstanding talent to perform the HKMA’s important functions, the HKMA is committed not only to green objectives but also to promoting the physical and mental well-being of its employees. In addition, through collaboration with stakeholders, we contribute to building a caring society by promoting financial inclusion, enhancing the public’s financial literacy and raising public awareness of financial fraud prevention. The climate challenge is immense and exceptionally urgent. As economies around the world move towards a more sustainable future, the process is expected to bring profound changes to financing activities and asset allocation. This transition entails significant risks, but it will also bring unprecedented opportunities. As a leading global sustainable finance hub, Hong Kong has a responsibility to take the lead in addressing these challenges. At the same time, we are well positioned to build on this momentum. The HKMA will fully support the industry in financing the low-carbon transition; continue to lead by example as a responsible investor and sustainable organisation; and work with like-minded partners to advance this critically important global agenda. Chief Executive Eddie Yue

Climate change risks and other sustainability issues are global concerns. The HKMA’s sustainability efforts aim to lead by example through its own policies and operations, ensure that Hong Kong’s financial system and the HKMA itself are resilient to the risks of climate change, and support the transition to a more sustainable economy. By actively participating in international and regional organisations, the HKMA will also seek to contribute to the formulation of regional and global green and sustainable finance policies and standards. As a banking regulator, the HKMA will further strengthen the banking sector’s climate resilience and climate risk management capabilities. Specifically, the key priorities include: conducting a new round of thematic examinations of banks’ climate risk management practices and a new round of consultation meetings as part of the review of banks’ progress in implementing the supervisory requirements on climate risk management; continuing the work of incorporating climate considerations into the HKMA’s supervisory review process; completing the second round of the industry-wide climate risk stress test, providing guidance to participating banks throughout the process, and sharing observations and lessons learned with the industry; enhancing sustainability disclosures, including by working with relevant local authorities to align the relevant requirements with the International Financial Reporting Standards Sustainability Disclosure Standards as the global baseline, and preparing for the implementation of the Basel Committee on Banking Supervision’s Pillar 31 framework for climate-related financial risks; and sharing guidance on best practices in transition planning with the industry. To foster the sound development of banks’ provision of green and sustainable investment products, the HKMA will continue to keep abreast of local and international market and regulatory developments and maintain close liaison with the industry to ensure that banks adopt appropriate selling processes. In addition, the HKMA will play a facilitative role in promoting the development of the green finance ecosystem and supporting banks in financing the economic transition. We will soon publish the local green taxonomy and continue to broaden its coverage to include more activities, such as transition activities. Meanwhile, we will continue to explore the use of technological solutions to help banks identify, measure and monitor their climate risk exposures; one example is the forthcoming cloud-based platform designed to facilitate banks’ physical risk assessments. To enhance practitioners’ professional capabilities, we will also develop the professional-level “Green and Sustainable Finance” module under the “Enhanced Competency Framework on Banking” in 2024. Hong Kong is well positioned to serve as a regional and international sustainable finance hub. To fulfil this role, the HKMA is assisting the Government in implementing the proposal in the 2023–24 Budget to expand the scope of the Government Green Bond Programme to cover sustainable finance projects, thereby deepening the development of the local green and sustainable debt market; while attracting more green financing activities, including transition finance activities, to Hong Kong through the Green and Sustainable Finance Grant Scheme. We will also continue to encourage more governments, institutions and corporates to raise green funds through Hong Kong, and explore potential synergies between green finance and technology. In addition, we will continue to assist in implementing the Government-funded Pilot Green and Sustainable Finance Capacity Building Support Scheme to expand Hong Kong’s green finance talent pool. As Co-Chair of the Green and Sustainable Finance Cross-Agency Steering Group (Steering Group), we will continue to work closely with other agencies to coordinate cross-sectoral policies and initiatives to promote the development of green and sustainable finance in Hong Kong. In 2024, the Steering Group will focus on three areas: sustainability disclosures, the application of technology, and transition finance. As another priority, through the Alliance for Green Commercial Banks, the HKMA and the International Finance Corporation will continue to jointly roll out various dedicated programmes in Asia, including conducting green finance research, providing distinctive market analysis and targeted professional training for banks, and offering practical guidance to support financial institutions in developing their own differentiated green transition pathways. In 2024, we will also seek to deepen collaboration with the Glasgow Financial Alliance for Net Zero, the Capacity-building Alliance of Sustainable Investment, and the Green Investment and Finance Partnership. As a responsible investor, the HKMA is committed to achieving net-zero emissions for the Exchange Fund’s “Investment Portfolio” by 2050 or earlier. We will continue to enhance the sustainability of the Exchange Fund’s investments through a three-pronged responsible investment approach, ensuring portfolio resilience throughout the journey towards net zero. Recognising that the objectives of the Paris Agreement can only be achieved through an economy-wide transition, we are refining our net-zero strategy to focus, subject to the Exchange Fund’s investment objectives, on assets that can deliver positive climate benefits to the real economy. As an environmentally responsible organisation, the HKMA’s decarbonisation strategy will continue to evolve to reflect the latest market, regulatory, technological and other climate-related developments. To further strengthen the HKMA’s climate resilience and risk preparedness, we will explore the feasibility of using technological solutions to assess the impact of physical risks on our offices. In addition, we will continue to actively encourage staff participation in our sustainability efforts, including launching campaigns to foster sustainable habits and enhancing office processes and practices. The HKMA will also continue to maintain a consistent, efficient and sustainable procurement approach, including assessing suppliers’ ESG practices when selecting suppliers and renewing contracts. Building on the green data centre certification obtained in 2023, the HKMA is committed to upholding the prescribed certification standards. In the regular upgrading of data centre facilities, we will incorporate green designs and practices in addition to keeping abreast of the latest technological developments. Meanwhile, we will continue to reduce electronic waste through the use of technology and convergence, and proactively modernise internal systems to improve efficiency and minimise potential risks. Finally, in the area of social focus, the HKMA will identify more community service opportunities for colleagues, and collaborate with the industry to promote financial inclusion and financial literacy, as well as enhance public awareness of financial fraud prevention.

Climate change affects every aspect of human life, and everyone can contribute to mitigating its impact. Through its multiple roles as a central banking institution, banking regulator, market facilitator, responsible investor and sustainable organisation, the HKMA contributes to promoting and accelerating the transition to net-zero emissions in Hong Kong and across Asia. The HKMA has established a robust sustainability governance framework to steer the formulation of its relevant strategies and policies, oversee the implementation of related initiatives, and ensure that sustainability considerations are integrated into its own operations and practices. In pursuit of good corporate governance, the HKMA has established a robust sustainability governance framework for its sustainability-related work, with clear accountability arrangements and a high degree of transparency. The governance framework ensures that sustainability considerations are effectively integrated into the HKMA’s strategic planning and decision-making processes, with effective mechanisms in place to monitor and evaluate the progress and effectiveness of its sustainability work. The HKMA’s sustainability governance framework comprises: the Exchange Fund Advisory Committee and its relevant sub-committees, which monitor and advise on the HKMA’s work, including its sustainability work; the Green and Sustainability Steering Committee (Steering Committee), chaired by the Chief Executive of the HKMA, which steers the HKMA’s overall environmental, social and governance (ESG) strategies and policies at the management level; in relation to responsible investment, the ESG Committee under the Exchange Fund Investment Office, which co-ordinates and oversees ESG-related work within the Exchange Fund Investment Office; and, for other functional areas, relevant teams and working groups, which plan and implement sustainability initiatives relating to banking and market development as well as the HKMA’s own operations. At the cross-sectoral level, the Green and Sustainable Finance Cross-Agency Steering Group (CASG), co-initiated by the HKMA and the Securities and Futures Commission (SFC), co-ordinates the efforts of financial regulators, government bureaux, industry stakeholders and other stakeholders to accelerate the development of green and sustainable finance in Hong Kong. Given the significant expansion in the scope of the HKMA’s sustainability work over the past few years, we established the Steering Committee in October as a new central platform to steer and more effectively co-ordinate all sustainability work across the HKMA’s different functional areas1. It provides guidance on the formulation of strategies, policies and plans for ESG-related matters across the four functional areas of banking, market development, Exchange Fund investment and internal operations; oversees the implementation of ESG-related plans by the HKMA’s various functional units; evaluates the HKMA’s performance and effectiveness in achieving its ESG objectives; and oversees its external communication strategy. The Steering Committee is chaired by the Chief Executive of the HKMA, with the three Deputy Chief Executives serving as standing members. Executive Directors responsible for key functions relevant to green and sustainability matters are also invited to attend Steering Committee meetings to report on the key outcomes of their work and future plans. The Steering Committee meets regularly and is supported by relevant working groups under the HKMA’s banking departments, Corporate Services, External and Investment Offices. In addition to formulating and implementing its own sustainability initiatives, the HKMA and the SFC jointly initiated the CASG2 in May 2020. As a cross-agency platform, the CASG provides strategic direction and co-ordinates cross-sectoral efforts by the financial sector to address climate and environmental risks, with a view to consolidating Hong Kong’s position as a leading green and sustainable finance centre in Asia and globally. For details of the CASG’s work, see the chapter “Strengthening the Green and Sustainable Finance Ecosystem”.

Climate change is an important risk facing the financial system. The HKMA has been working to strengthen Hong Kong’s financial system to build a greener and more sustainable future, contributing to Hong Kong’s climate goals and the global sustainable development agenda. Banks are affected by various sustainability- and climate-related issues in their day-to-day business operations. To continue performing their important functions in the financial system and channel more capital into green and sustainable projects, banks must proactively manage climate risk. As the banking regulator, the HKMA places particular emphasis on building banks’ capabilities to address and manage climate risk, and accelerating their efforts to support the transition to a low-carbon economy. The HKMA is committed to developing various policy measures to enhance the banking system’s resilience to climate risk. In August, the HKMA issued a circular on net-zero transition planning, setting out high-level principles to assist banks in maintaining safety and soundness during the transition of the economy towards net-zero emissions. Following the issuance of the circular, we conducted a questionnaire survey of selected banks in the fourth quarter to understand their transition planning practices. Based on the survey results, we will share observations and best practices on transition planning with the industry, and organise seminars or workshops to facilitate the exchange of experience within the industry. Regarding disclosure requirements, in light of the latest international developments, including the publication of the IFRS Sustainability Disclosure Standards in June and the Basel Committee on Banking Supervision’s (Basel Committee) consultation on a Pillar 3 disclosure framework for climate-related financial risks in November, the HKMA is stepping up efforts to refine the sustainability-related disclosure framework for banks in Hong Kong. Specifically, the HKMA is collaborating with relevant local authorities and stakeholders to develop a comprehensive roadmap for Hong Kong that is aligned with the IFRS Sustainability Disclosure Standards. During the year, the HKMA strengthened its supervision of banks’ climate risk management and provided recommendations to help banks further enhance their climate resilience and climate risk management capabilities. The HKMA made significant progress in implementing its two-year plan to incorporate climate risk factors into the banking supervisory process. Climate risk management has now become a standing agenda item at prudential meetings with bank management. Banking supervisors also assess banks’ risk profiles and risk management systems using an enhanced CAMEL rating system1 that incorporates climate risk factors. As part of implementing the two-year plan to incorporate climate risk factors into the banking supervisory process, the HKMA revised the “greenness” assessment framework to focus on banks’ transition planning practices. The HKMA is also reviewing the supervisory review process used to assess and monitor banks’ capital adequacy and determine their Pillar 2 capital requirements, with a view to encouraging banks to enhance their risk management frameworks to address climate risk. Key work priorities in 2023 under the two-year plan Following the end of the 12-month implementation period for compliance with Supervisory Policy Manual module GS-1 “Climate Risk Management”, the HKMA commenced a round of thematic reviews on climate-related risk governance in the second quarter. The thematic review covered four major areas, namely the governance structure for climate-related risks, oversight of climate strategies, oversight of climate-related risk management, and institutional culture, awareness and communication. The HKMA made various enhancements to the climate risk stress test framework, including introducing a new five-year scenario to assess the potential impact on banks of concurrent economic and climate change shocks. Following these enhancements, and as part of the HKMA’s regular programme of regulator-led stress tests, the second round of climate risk stress tests commenced in June to conduct a comprehensive assessment of banks’ climate risk exposures and further enhance their capabilities to manage climate risk. A total of 44 banks participated in this stress test, representing an increase of more than 60% compared with the first pilot exercise in 2021. The HKMA also organised a climate risk stress test forum in November, attended by as many as 300 banking practitioners. By facilitating experience-sharing among banks, the event helped deepen the industry’s overall understanding of climate risk measurement. The HKMA also conducted a series of consultation meetings to review banks’ progress in implementing the HKMA’s Supervisory Policy Manual module GS-1 “Climate Risk Management”. The HKMA met with bank management to discuss their climate risk management efforts and common challenges facing the industry, and reviewed information provided by banks and other publicly available information to assess their progress. The HKMA provided banks with targeted recommendations, encouraging and supporting them to continue enhancing their climate risk management capabilities in line with the HKMA’s supervisory expectations. As global attention to climate change and efforts to address it continue to grow, the HKMA has observed rising demand for green and sustainable investment products, with some banks offering such products to meet customer demand. In view of this, the HKMA completed a thematic review of banks’ sale of green and sustainable investment products and issued a circular in November setting out the standards banks are expected to meet and sharing good practices observed. Covering various areas including product due diligence, disclosure, governance and controls, staff training, and book and record keeping, the circular aims to mitigate potential greenwashing risks and strengthen investor confidence, thereby fostering the sound development of such investment activities. The HKMA will continue to monitor the latest trends and market developments. The HKMA is committed to promoting the application of technology in green and sustainable banking. For example, technology can improve data availability and risk analytics, thereby strengthening banks’ capabilities to manage climate risk. The HKMA will soon launch a pilot cloud-based platform for banks to assess the impact of physical risks on residential and commercial buildings under different climate scenarios. In addition, the HKMA continued to collaborate with other central banks and regulators to explore how technology solutions could assist in physical risk assessments. The HKMA also encourages the adoption of sustainable approaches to anti-money laundering (AML) through the application of advanced analytics and artificial intelligence, reducing the consumption of compliance-related resources. In 2023, the HKMA launched an online shared data submission platform that fully automates the collection of financial crime risk data, thereby enhancing banks’ operational processes for the sustainable submission of AML-related data. In September, the HKMA organised the “Green Fintech Competition” to identify market-ready solutions that could help the banking industry address challenges in the following areas: (i) net-zero transition or transition planning; (ii) climate risk management; (iii) green and sustainable finance; and (iv) sustainability- or climate-related disclosure and reporting. The competition attracted more than 85 submissions from around 70 companies. In December, the HKMA organised the “Green and Sustainable Banking Conference”, providing a platform for the banking and technology sectors to explore the roles of low-carbon technologies and green fintech in the net-zero transition of Hong Kong and the Mainland, while also announcing the results of the “Green Fintech Competition”. The event attracted around 400 participants from banks, technology companies, regulators and academia. To increase transparency across financial markets and promote greater consistency in green and sustainable finance decision-making, the HKMA developed a local green classification framework with the assistance of a consultancy firm. In May, the HKMA published a discussion paper on the “Prototype of a Green Classification Framework for Hong Kong”, seeking stakeholders’ views on establishing and implementing a green taxonomy. Based on the consultation results, the HKMA is fine-tuning the prototype framework and identifying additional areas for the next phase of its development. The HKMA participates in the work of the Financial Action Task Force, which has identified environmental crime as a predicate offence for money laundering. Given the interlinkages between AML and environmental, social and governance (ESG), this area is attracting increasing attention from regulators. Recognising the potential risks that climate change may pose to the financial system, the HKMA has incorporated a broader range of climate factors and scenarios into its analysis and research on financial vulnerabilities to strengthen its ongoing surveillance work. The HKMA takes climate change into account in its ongoing monitoring of financial stability risks and includes analyses of climate-related risks in its financial stability reports. Through its active participation in the Scenario Design and Analysis Workstream under the Network of Central Banks and Supervisors for Greening the Financial System (NGFS), the HKMA helped further enrich climate scenarios, enabling central banks and regulators to gain a clearer understanding of the macroeconomic and financial impacts of climate change. As a member of the Financial Stability Board’s working group on transition planning, the HKMA participated in analysing the interactions between the transition plans of financial and non-financial companies and financial stability, enabling policymakers to develop a forward-looking and dynamic perspective for examining climate-related financial risks. On the research front, the HKMA conducted various applied research projects to explore the impact of climate change and broader ESG issues on the financial industry and the economy. Research topics included the climate risk exposures of the banking industry and investment funds2, ESG fund flows3, the impact of climate change on property prices4, and the ripple effects of corporate ESG performance across global supply chains5. The findings of these studies enhanced the HKMA’s understanding of the implications of climate change and ESG issues for financial stability, supporting the formulation of relevant policies. Domestically, these studies helped strengthen the HKMA’s ongoing monitoring and assessment of the impact of climate risk on financial stability. Externally, the HKMA also shared its research findings with a broad range of stakeholders through international events on climate-related issues, the HKMA Research Memorandum series and other channels. The HKMA’s “Liquidity Facilities Framework” is a collateralised standby funding arrangement that provides timely liquidity support to banks in need. In accordance with the NGFS’s recommendations, the HKMA has incorporated sustainability considerations into the assessment of eligible collateral under this framework. The HKMA actively participates in international and regional discussions on addressing climate risk and mainstreaming sustainable finance. Through such participation, the HKMA helps promote international and regional policy dialogue on addressing climate change and its impact on financial stability, while drawing insights to strengthen the climate resilience of Hong Kong’s financial system.

To reinforce Hong Kong’s position as a leading green and sustainable finance hub in the region, the HKMA is committed to raising market awareness and participation, providing the necessary infrastructure and enablers, and supporting international initiatives to align with global standards. During the year, the HKMA worked closely with local and international partners to build a richer ecosystem and further advance green and sustainable finance in Hong Kong. The Green and Sustainable Finance Cross-Agency Steering Group (Steering Group), co-chaired by the HKMA and the Securities and Futures Commission (SFC), coordinates the financial sector’s response to climate and environmental risks, accelerates the development of green and sustainable finance in Hong Kong, and supports the Government’s climate strategies. The Steering Group has made good progress since its establishment. In January 2024, the Steering Group announced key initiatives to support Hong Kong in capitalising on sustainable finance opportunities, with major workstreams covering sustainability disclosures, ecosystem building, transition finance and green fintech. Specifically, a Sustainability Disclosures Working Group was established to develop a roadmap for adopting the IFRS Sustainability Disclosure Standards in Hong Kong. The roadmap will cover four key areas, namely sustainability reporting, assurance, data and technology, and skills training. A Transition Finance Working Group was also established to explore ways to support financial institutions and corporates in transition planning and reporting. The Steering Group also strengthened the sustainable finance ecosystem through cross-sectoral skills training and data enhancement. In particular, on data, we continued to promote the adoption of the climate and environmental risk questionnaire2 for non-listed companies launched by the Steering Group in collaboration with CDP in 2022. The Steering Group will continue to keep abreast of the latest developments in green and sustainable finance and enhance Hong Kong’s position as a regional and global green and sustainable finance hub. In January 2024, the Steering Group announced three new key initiatives to capitalise on the financing and investment opportunities arising from the low-carbon transition in the Asia-Pacific region. To support skills training for the industry, the Centre for Green and Sustainable Finance under the Steering Group implemented the Government’s Pilot Green and Sustainable Finance Capacity Building Support Scheme, which provides subsidies to practitioners, students and graduates undertaking green and sustainable finance-related training and acquiring relevant qualifications. As of December 2023, a total of 46 international and local training programmes or qualifications had been registered as eligible programmes or qualifications under the Scheme, and more than 560 subsidy applications had been approved. The HKMA also launched the foundation level of a new “Green and Sustainable Finance” module under the Enhanced Competency Framework for Banking Practitioners. The module aims to promote talent development in the banking sector and enhance the overall professional competence of practitioners. In 2024, the HKMA will continue to work with the banking industry to develop the professional level of the module to meet the industry’s rapidly growing demand for green and sustainable finance professionals. To help financial institutions and corporates, especially small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs), better understand key climate- and sustainability-related issues, including climate risk management, sustainability reporting, greenhouse gas emissions calculation and transition planning, the HKMA collaborated during the year with relevant Government bureaux and departments, as well as global partners such as CDP, the Glasgow Financial Alliance for Net Zero (GFANZ)3 and the Partnership for Carbon Accounting Financials (PCAF)4, to organise a series of seminars and thematic workshops, attracting participants from the financial services and corporate sectors. For students, following the launch of the Sustainable Finance Internship Initiative in 2022, training sessions were held in January and February 2023 to deepen interns’ and university bachelor’s degree graduates’ understanding of sustainable finance. Recognising the potential of technology to bridge climate-related data gaps and improve data quality, the HKMA is committed to making such data more accessible and enhancing its quality to support informed decision-making and effective climate action. In February 2024, the Steering Group launched a series of website enhancements to provide financial institutions, corporates and the public with one-stop access to green and sustainable finance information. Key enhancements included an electronic sustainability disclosure platform, greenhouse gas emissions calculation and estimation tools, and more centralised, user-friendly and searchable data and resources. During “Hong Kong Green Week”, the Steering Group also co-organised the “Unlocking Sustainability through Tech” event with Cyberport and Invest Hong Kong to showcase leading green innovation solutions and Hong Kong’s strengths in green technology. “Hong Kong Green Week – Finance Stream” was held from 26 February to 1 March 2024, during which various sustainability-themed events attracted more than 1,600 guests from nearly 30 regions, including representatives from financial institutions, corporates, central banks, international organisations, government agencies, academia and consultancy firms. The highlight of “Hong Kong Green Week” was the “Climate Business Forum: Asia Pacific”, co-organised by the HKMA and the International Finance Corporation. The Forum brought together more than 400 guests, including leading decision-makers from the global business and financial sectors, to discuss solutions for unlocking climate finance in the Asia-Pacific region. The two-day event explored a wide range of topics, including energy transition, decarbonisation of heavy industries, the circular economy, the future development of sustainable finance, and emerging climate technologies in emerging and developing markets in the Asia-Pacific region. With support from public- and private-sector organisations, more than 10 roundtables, seminars and other networking events were co-organised. Topics covered climate finance, carbon markets, electric vehicle supply chains, financing the net-zero transition, green taxonomies and financing green development in Belt and Road regions. In addition, the HKMA and the International Monetary Fund co-organised the “Roundtable on Climate Finance in Asia” on 29 February 2024 to explore key measures for scaling up climate finance and the roles of central banks and regulators in climate risk management. These events formed part of the HKMA’s overall efforts to foster and enrich Hong Kong’s green and sustainable finance ecosystem, serving as useful platforms for participants to drive new business development, share knowledge and explore new opportunities to address climate finance challenges in the Asia-Pacific region. The HKMA has also been actively supporting the development of green and sustainable finance in the region. In November 2020, the International Finance Corporation and the HKMA launched the Alliance for Green Commercial Banks5 as a collaborative platform bringing together regional financial institutions, banking industry associations, research institutions and innovative technology providers to jointly develop green commercial banking. Since March 2021, the Alliance has held a total of 22 training events and roundtables, attracting more than 7,300 participants from around the world, including the Asia-Pacific region, Europe, the Middle East, Africa and the Americas. In October, the Alliance and Crédit Agricole CIB published their second thought leadership report, titled “Climate Strategy for Banks: Developing an Ambitious Plan to Address Climate Change – Case Studies”. In October, the Alliance and Crédit Agricole CIB jointly published the thought leadership report “Climate Strategy for Banks: Developing an Ambitious Plan to Address Climate Change – Case Studies”. During the year, the HKMA Infrastructure Financing Facilitation Office joined the newly established Capacity-building Alliance of Sustainable Investment (CASI) and the Green Investment and Finance Partnership (GIFP) initiated by the Belt and Road Initiative International Green Development Coalition. Collaboration with CASI and GIFP will facilitate capacity building and knowledge sharing, and channel more capital towards green and sustainable projects in Asia and beyond. In August 2023, GFANZ announced the establishment of its Hong Kong Chapter to support the net-zero efforts of financial institutions in Hong Kong and the Mainland. The HKMA supports GFANZ’s work in an advisory capacity. To demonstrate the Government’s commitment to combating climate change, promoting green finance and developing Hong Kong into a more sustainable and liveable city, the Government launched the Government Green Bond Programme in 2018. The HKMA assists with the issuance of green bonds under the Programme. To date, the Government has issued approximately US$25 billion equivalent of institutional and retail green bonds, with the proceeds allocated to more than 70 green government projects, such as green buildings, waste management and resource recovery, energy efficiency and conservation. To enhance the Programme’s transparency and accountability, the Government publishes a Green Bond Report annually, setting out in detail the allocation of green bond proceeds and the expected environmental benefits. The Government continued its regular institutional green bond issuance programme in the 2023-24 financial year and issued approximately US$6 billion equivalent of green bonds in June. The triple-currency offering comprised US dollar-, euro- and renminbi-denominated bonds of different tenors, attracting different types of investors and receiving an enthusiastic response, with subscriptions totalling nearly US$30 billion equivalent. The issuance size of the renminbi bonds increased from RMB10 billion in January to RMB15 billion, and a 10-year renminbi bond was introduced for the first time, helping to extend the Government’s renminbi yield curve and further enrich the range of offshore renminbi (CNH) products. The enthusiastic response from global investors to the Government’s green bond offerings reflected their recognition of Hong Kong’s commitment to promoting green and sustainable development. In October, the Government issued a second batch of green retail bonds totalling Hong Kong dollar (HKD) 20 billion, further promoting market development and financial inclusion. The offering provided members of the public with an investment opportunity offering stable returns, enabling them both to participate in and benefit from the development of green finance in Hong Kong.

As an important global asset owner and manager, the HKMA plays a pivotal role in promoting the development of green and sustainable finance in support of the global climate agenda. The HKMA has long been a pioneer in responsible investment. Since 2015, the HKMA has led the way in investing in green and sustainable assets, requiring its external managers to exercise active ownership and integrate environmental, social and governance factors into the investment management of the Exchange Fund. Guided by the principle of “Capital Preservation First, Long-Term Growth Next”1, the HKMA invests prudently and believes that due consideration of environmental, social and governance (ESG) factors helps mitigate the associated investment risks while unlocking the long-term sustainable value of investments. As one of the first central banks to sign the Principles for Responsible Investment (PRI) and set a “Net-zero by 2050” target2 for its “Investment Portfolio”, the HKMA is committed to advancing its responsible investment journey continuously, with an emphasis on sustainability, particularly the pressing issue of climate change, with a view to enhancing the resilience of the Exchange Fund and achieving better risk-adjusted long-term returns. As a responsible investor, the HKMA contributes to building a robust green and sustainable finance ecosystem, partnering with like-minded investors, regulators and international organisations to formulate industry standards and promote the adoption of responsible investment across the financial sector and central banking community. Through stewardship and collaborative initiatives, the HKMA strives to foster a future in which finance and sustainable development go hand in hand. Figure 1 The Exchange Fund’s responsible investment journey Comprehensive and reliable ESG information is essential for integrating sustainability and planning a credible climate transition towards net-zero targets. To fulfil its commitments to support the Network for Greening the Financial System (NGFS) Glasgow Declaration3 and the strategic plan of the Green and Sustainable Finance Cross-Agency Steering Group, the HKMA leads by example by preparing this chapter on the Exchange Fund’s responsible investment in accordance with the recommendations of the Task Force on Climate-related Financial Disclosures (TCFD). The Exchange Fund Advisory Committee, chaired by the Financial Secretary, establishes the responsible investment framework and guiding principles, which are implemented by the Exchange Fund Investment Office in the investment management of the Exchange Fund. The overarching guiding principle sets the tone for the HKMA to practise responsible investment while meeting the investment objectives of the Exchange Fund. The Investment Sub-Committee under the Exchange Fund Advisory Committee, chaired by the Chief Executive of the HKMA, oversees ESG and climate-related risks relating to the Exchange Fund’s investments. The Investment Sub-Committee reviews the responsible investment framework and risk management approach, and monitors their implementation through regular meeting reports from the Sustainable Investment Team of the Exchange Fund Investment Office. As shown in Figure 2, the ESG Committee under the Exchange Fund Investment Office, chaired by the Chief Strategy Officer, co-ordinates and oversees the Exchange Fund Investment Office’s ESG initiatives. Proposals and work progress discussed at the ESG Committee’s quarterly meetings are reported to the Chief Executive Officer of the Exchange Fund Investment Office. In addition, the Green and Sustainable Steering Committee, chaired by the Chief Executive of the HKMA and attended by the Chief Executive Officer and Chief Strategy Officer of the Exchange Fund Investment Office, meets semi-annually to provide guidance on ESG policies and initiatives across different functions of the HKMA, including the Exchange Fund Investment Office, in pursuit of the HKMA’s overall ESG objectives. Figure 2 Responsible investment governance structure of the Exchange Fund Investment Office As shown in Figure 1, the Exchange Fund Investment Office embarked on its responsible investment journey in 2016, initially focusing on managing ESG risks that could affect the financial performance of the Exchange Fund. As sustainable development evolved rapidly and moved beyond risk considerations to become a strategic priority for leading institutions worldwide, the Exchange Fund Investment Office revisited its responsible investment approach. July 2023 marked another milestone, when the Exchange Fund Investment Office established a new Business Strategy Department led by the Chief Strategy Officer to co-ordinate and lead its strategic development, incorporating the responsible investment task force formerly under the Risk Management and Compliance Division—now known as the Sustainable Investment Team. This strategic realignment reflects the HKMA’s shift in responsible investment from a risk-based focus to a more proactive and forward-looking stance in addressing sustainability-related investment matters. The Sustainable Investment Team works closely with different teams within the Exchange Fund Investment Office on ESG integration and assists its senior management in managing ESG risks and opportunities, particularly those related to climate, across different types of investments: Public market investments—The Credit, Regulations and Compliance Committee, comprising senior management of the Exchange Fund Investment Office, reviews the integration of ESG factors into credit risk models with reference to the Sustainable Investment Team’s input, and monitors the ESG profile of fixed-income portfolios through regular reporting by the Risk Management and Compliance Division. In addition, the Sustainable Investment Team participates from an ESG perspective in the selection, appointment and monitoring of external managers for equity portfolios (see “Promoting active ownership” under “Risk Management” on page 40 for details). Private market investments—The Investment Sub-Committee, chaired by the Chief Executive of the HKMA, considers ESG-related assessments of each investment proposal conducted by the private market investment and risk management teams. The HKMA recognises that the physical and transition risks4 posed by climate change, as well as the related opportunities, may affect the long-term performance and value of the Exchange Fund’s investments. The Emissions Gap Report 20235 published by the United Nations Environment Programme estimates that, unless further reductions in greenhouse gas emissions are made globally, the average global temperature will rise by 2.5 to 2.9 degrees Celsius above pre-industrial levels by 2030. The urgent need for more aggressive policies, technological development or behavioural change to contain temperature increases may exacerbate transition risks, such as shocks from asset depreciation or stranded assets. Meanwhile, the increasing frequency and severity of extreme weather events also pose additional physical risks to investments. The HKMA believes that investing in a greener future is aligned with the investment objectives of the Exchange Fund, and therefore places particular emphasis on climate-related factors in ESG integration. The HKMA’s establishment in 2022 of a target for the Exchange Fund’s “Investment Portfolio” to achieve net-zero emissions by 2050 or earlier further demonstrated its commitment to the global climate agenda. The HKMA continues to strengthen its three-pronged approach, with a clear focus on decarbonisation and transition. The following sections elaborate on this approach. Figure 3 The HKMA’s three-pronged approach to responsible investment In pursuing its net-zero target, the HKMA favours active engagement over exclusion or divestment from its investment universe. First, maintaining a diversified and robust asset portfolio is critical to achieving the Exchange Fund’s primary investment objectives. The outright exclusion of certain sectors or industries would narrow the investable universe, with potential implications for investment returns and risks. Through an inclusive approach, the HKMA can capture opportunities to invest in companies that are undergoing transition and possess superior technologies and sound corporate governance to respond to evolving global climate trends, including companies in high-emitting industries. Second, tackling climate change requires the transition of core “brown” industries. Merely excluding or divesting from the relevant investments would not resolve the issue of carbon emissions. Instead, through the deployment of strategic capital and active ownership, the HKMA supports these industries in transitioning to sustainable and low-carbon practices, thereby driving positive change for themselves and the world. In response to market developments, the HKMA is refining its net-zero investment strategy to pursue, through a holistic approach, transition outcomes that align with the net-zero objectives of both the Exchange Fund and the world, while adhering to its guiding principles for responsible investment. By integrating ESG factors into investment decisions, the HKMA continues to pursue sustainable investments and opportunities to facilitate climate transition and enhance the long-term resilience of the Exchange Fund’s portfolios (Figure 4). The HKMA’s responsible investment maintained strong momentum in 2023. In the public markets, the HKMA launched a new actively managed global equity portfolio themed around sustainability and climate transition, managed by external managers, and extended the application of a customised low-carbon equity index to another externally managed portfolio. In addition, the green, social and sustainability bonds prioritised by the HKMA outperformed their investment benchmarks, demonstrating the concept of “doing well by doing good”. In the private markets, the HKMA actively builds resilient portfolios for long-term growth, capturing investment opportunities expected to benefit from long-term economic trends such as climate and energy transition. For example, during the year the HKMA invested in two Asia-focused transition investment funds, demonstrating its commitment to addressing Asia’s climate transition needs. Figure 4 Ongoing initiatives to promote ESG investment The HKMA has invested in a company specialising in producing environmentally friendly thermoplastic materials from unsorted household waste, including organic matter such as food waste, and non-recyclable materials. Unlike conventional chemical recycling systems that rely on energy-intensive high-temperature environments to produce plastics, the company has pioneered a low-temperature production method powered entirely by solar arrays. This plastic material, made 100% from waste, offers a sustainable and versatile alternative to petroleum-based resins commonly used in industries such as retail and consumer durables. It is also compatible with existing standard manufacturing processes and cutting-edge technologies such as 3D printing. The company is a staunch supporter of the circular economy. The HKMA committed two tranches of US$1 billion each to the MCPP in 2017 and 2019 respectively, and further collaborated with the International Finance Corporation in 2021 to create a new global climate-related investment platform, “MCPP One Planet”, which is also the world’s first cross-sectoral emerging market loan portfolio aligned with the Paris Agreement. Through the MCPP programme, the HKMA has committed to provide loans to 80 sustainable development projects across 19 sectors, including infrastructure, agriculture, real estate and manufacturing, in 38 developing countries. The International Finance Corporation collected data relating to the MCPP loans. According to its report, the HKMA’s loan commitments have supported emerging markets and developing countries in various areas, including economic transformation and human capital development. Specifically, the projects financed by the HKMA are expected to reduce greenhouse gas emissions by approximately 5.6 million tonnes of carbon dioxide equivalent annually, equivalent to the greenhouse gas emissions from an average gasoline-powered car travelling 14 billion miles. The HKMA actively collaborates with like-minded investors and partners to promote responsible investment and enhance industry capabilities.

The HKMA is committed to becoming a sustainable organisation and adopts a multi-pronged approach to reducing its carbon footprint, with the goal of achieving net-zero emissions by 2050 or earlier. In addition to promoting environmental sustainability, the HKMA attaches importance to staff well-being and social responsibility, and strives to promote financial inclusion and enhance the public’s financial literacy. As a responsible organisation, the HKMA has set sustainability goals under the three pillars of the environment, staff and social responsibility. Established in October, the Green and Sustainability Steering Committee (Steering Committee)1, chaired by the Chief Executive of the HKMA, is the principal decision-making body for the HKMA’s corporate sustainability initiatives. Formerly known as the Corporate Social Responsibility and Sustainability Committee, the Steering Committee leads the HKMA in formulating its vision, strategies and policies on corporate sustainability and social responsibility matters. At the departmental level, the Executive Director (Corporate Services) oversees the implementation of sustainability activities and submits regular progress reports to the Steering Committee. The Green Office Box and the Volunteer Services Group support the co-ordination of corporate sustainability work; the former serves as a platform for brainstorming ways to create a green working environment, while the latter aims to foster a culture of participation in volunteer activities. The HKMA has developed a roadmap to guide its transition. The focus is on implementing decarbonisation strategies in its daily operations, including operating green buildings and data centres, practising green travel, adopting energy-saving measures, digital tools and more environmentally friendly operating practices, reducing waste, and building a culture of sustainability. The HKMA also plans to use carbon insetting tools within its own value chain to reduce emissions, while using carbon offsets for hard-to-abate emissions. In addition to the above environmental commitments relating to its daily operations, the HKMA continues to introduce greener operational solutions for the wider community, ranging from channels for banks to submit electronic documents and communicate with the HKMA to electronic payment and coin collection schemes for the general public. To strengthen and sustain its operational capabilities, the HKMA employs a professional workforce, builds a talent pool and places emphasis on staff well-being.
