The HKMA has also been monitoring its exposure to transition risks by tracking greenhouse gas emissions and waste generated by its operations, as well as energy and paper consumption. The HKMA’s latest climate target is to achieve net-zero Scope 1, Scope 2 and Scope 3 greenhouse gas emissions associated with its corporate operations by 2030. These targets were developed with reference to the Science Based Targets initiative methodology. The HKMA adopts the Greenhouse Gas Protocol to measure and report its corporate emissions. Scope 1 emissions are direct emissions from petrol vehicles. Given the nature of its operations, the HKMA’s principal greenhouse gas emissions are Scope 2 indirect greenhouse gas emissions arising from the consumption of electricity generated using fossil fuels. In the absence of supplier-specific data, the HKMA adopts a conservative approach to estimating major Scope 3 emissions from purchased goods, including capital goods, and services. Other relevant Scope 3 emissions include waste sent to landfills and staff air travel and commuting. Detailed calculations for 2023 and 2024 are set out in the “Performance Summary” on page 50. The performance data disclosed by the HKMA have been independently verified by the Hong Kong Quality Assurance Agency. The scope and criteria of its verification are set out in the “Verification Statement” appended to the end of this report. The HKMA leads by example, adhering to the same climate-related standards that it expects the banks it regulates and the financial system it oversees to follow. As a first step towards green mobility, the HKMA began replacing its petrol vehicles with electric vehicles in 2024 and will continue this work in 2025 to achieve fully green mobility. The HKMA continues to incorporate environmental considerations into the design, operation, repair and maintenance of its offices. Specifically, in various renovation projects in 2024, the HKMA reused existing furniture and fitting-out materials or traded in old items for new ones to reduce waste. To enhance overall energy efficiency, the HKMA regularly reviews energy consumption and energy-saving measures in its offices and data centres. In a data centre facility upgrade project in 2024, it adopted a modular uninterruptible power supply system to further optimise the Power Usage Effectiveness (PUE) of its BEAM Plus-certified data centre. The design allows flexible capacity expansion, enhances operating efficiency under partial loads, and incorporates advanced cooling technology and higher power density, helping reduce overall energy consumption. The HKMA enhances internal virtual collaboration through its digital workplace, coupled with streamlined workflows, effectively reducing paper consumption. In addition, the HKMA extends the service lives of mobile and desktop devices with reference to manufacturers’ software update cycles, thereby extending the period during which the devices can be used securely. To reduce office waste, the HKMA follows the “4R” principles of refuse, reduce, reuse and recycle, and conducts regular waste audits to help formulate targeted waste management strategies. Recycling bins for different materials are placed at convenient locations throughout the offices. To increase the recycling rate, the HKMA added recycling bins for beverage cartons and plastic fruit netting in 2024. In addition, since November 2022, the HKMA has sent collected food waste to a waste-to-energy facility in Hong Kong. In May 2024, the HKMA joined the Environmental Protection Department’s Waste Reduction Pledge for Events, committing to measures to reduce waste generated by various events. The HKMA continues to prioritise the procurement of goods that meet the environmental specifications in the Government’s Green Procurement List, particularly electrical appliances and office consumables. To reduce carbon emissions from air travel, the HKMA encourages staff to plan trips carefully, such as by combining multiple trips wherever possible when attending overseas events. At the corporate level, the HKMA has purchased sustainable aviation fuel since 2023, reducing annual carbon emissions from air travel by approximately 10%. In addition, the HKMA participates in Gold Standard-certified carbon offsetting programmes to offset the remaining carbon emissions from air travel; these programmes focus on renewable energy production and electrification projects in emerging markets. In 2024, the HKMA arranged various learning activities for staff, such as seminars and guided tours of waste-to-energy facilities, to enhance their understanding of environmental sustainability issues. From Earth Day on 22 April 2024 through the end of May, the HKMA held its first “HKMA Green Month” under the theme “Think Green, Live Green, Work Green”. It provided a valuable opportunity to demonstrate the HKMA’s commitment to and momentum in embedding environmental sustainability into its internal operations. The programme included a “Sustainability BINGO Scorecard” encouraging staff to practise green living, a “Save the Earth” quiz, and a workshop on caring for “kokedama” indoor plants originating from Japan; waste audit results were also shared, while an operator of a community recycling centre introduced recycling best practices. To sustain the momentum of Green Month, the HKMA launched an approximately six-month recycling campaign in October, highlighting responsible waste disposal and reminding staff that the cumulative effect of small changes in individual habits could significantly improve the organisation’s overall recycling performance. One highlight of the campaign was the launch of the “Green in Action” video, in which senior executives shared recycling tips. The campaign also introduced a series of screen savers, eye-catching posters, intranet articles and electronic prompts to remind staff to take action to reduce waste and increase recycling. At the end of 2024, the HKMA conducted a staff survey to gauge their awareness of sustainability and collect their views on proposed green office initiatives. The survey results will help shape future sustainability training activities and waste management strategies. As Hong Kong’s central banking institution, the HKMA regards itself as an important agent of change and is therefore committed to leading efforts to accelerate the low-carbon transition and promote sustainable operating practices across the financial industry and society as a whole. The HKMA has introduced various initiatives to enhance the efficiency of external processes. Following the successful launch of the Common Data Submission Platform in 2023, the HKMA extended its coverage in 2024 to non-bank institutions, such as stored value facility operators, to facilitate their submission of certain regulatory data. The expanded platform coverage aims to further streamline submission processes for reporting institutions, provide a smoother experience for all users, and reinforce the HKMA’s commitment to sustainability. Other new initiatives launched in 2024 included SurveyTool, which enables banks to respond to HKMA surveys through a streamlined submission process, and the Smart Information and Document Management System, a centralised platform offering users advanced functions for searching documents related to banks.

Hong Kong Quality Assurance Agency conducted an independent verification of the environmental data (the “Data”) of the Hong Kong Monetary Authority (“HKMA”). The Data include total energy consumption, Scope 1 and Scope 2 greenhouse gas emissions, paper consumption, non-hazardous waste generated (including general waste sent to landfill and recyclable waste), greenhouse gas emissions from air travel, and their respective intensities for 2024. In addition, the Data include Scope 3 greenhouse gas emissions from purchased goods and services, capital goods, fuel- and energy-related activities, non-hazardous waste (including general waste sent to landfill and recyclable waste), and employee commuting, together with their corresponding intensities, for 2023 and 2024. HKMA’s greenhouse gas emissions data were prepared in accordance with the Greenhouse Gas Protocol (“GHG Protocol”), jointly published by the World Resources Institute and the World Business Council of Sustainable Development. The verification scope covered a total of 6 office and warehouse assets, comprising 5 offices located at 1) Two International Finance Centre, 2) Hopewell Centre, 3) One Pacific Place, 4) Kowloon Commerce Centre, and 5) International Commerce Centre, and a warehouse at 6) Roxy Industrial Centre in Kwai Chung. The objective of the verification was to provide reasonable assurance as to the accuracy and reliability of the Data and to confirm the adequacy of HKMA’s data collection mechanism. Within the verification scope, Hong Kong Quality Assurance Agency reviewed selected representative data and supporting evidence from the 6 assets. The verification was conducted in accordance with International Standard on Assurance Engagements 3000 (Revised), “Assurance Engagements Other than Audits or Reviews of Historical Financial Information”, issued by the International Auditing and Assurance Standards Board. The verification procedures were designed to form an opinion and conclusion with a reasonable level of assurance. The verification process was determined in accordance with the requirements of the GHG Protocol. The verification process tested the completeness and accuracy of the Data by tracing selected sample data to their sources, and also reviewed the underlying procedures for data collection, aggregation, estimation, calculation and internal checking and performed reliability tests. The verification process also included verification of internal data collection and management mechanisms, interviews with representatives responsible for preparing the Data, and the selection of representative data and information for examination. Relevant source data and supporting evidence were also reviewed in detail during the verification process. HKMA is responsible for the collection and reporting of the Data. Our verification work was entirely independent and impartial. The Hong Kong Quality Assurance Agency verification team was not involved in the Data preparation process. Based on the results of this verification, Hong Kong Quality Assurance Agency provides reasonable assurance over the Data and concludes that: - the Data are materially accurate and reliable; - HKMA’s overall data collection mechanism is adequate.
